title: Polydispersity Index of Polymers Revealed by DOSY
abstract: The polydispersity index (PDI) of a polymer sample is a very important feature. It can reflect the purity of a standard sample or even modulate the physico-chemical properties of a polymer. The PDI is the ratio of the weight average molar mass (Mw) of the sample to its number average molar mass (Mn). NMR is a very useful tool to characterize polymers. Although ILT (Inverse Laplace Transform) analysis of DOSY (Diffusion-Ordered Spectroscopy) experiments was proposed to study mass distributions [1,2], no convincing method to measure PDI has been developed yet.
